clue.text: Recurring tea dance

indicators.note: something recurring comes round again, so the word for tea is given twice in a row

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A tea dance that is held again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurring' tells you to write CHA (slang for tea) twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom step, so it is one kind of dance.

clue.text: Offhand sort of labourer?

definitions.meaning: relaxed and unconcerned, careless in manner
a worker hired on a temporary, irregular basis rather than as permanent staff

explanation.definitionFit: The word means nonchalant and also describes a worker employed temporarily, a double definition.

clue.text: Cas steers around performers

indicators.note: around suggests moving letters about, so the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Cas drives a car around some actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cas' looks like a person's name, but it is just letters for the anagram signalled by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are women who act on stage or screen, so they are examples of performers.

clue.text: Television presenter in Soho street

indicators.note: in tells you the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A TV presenter spotted in a street in Soho, the London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters running across 'Soho street'; Soho is a London entertainment district.
explanation.definitionFit: A host introduces guests and runs a television programme, so the word means a TV presenter.

clue.text: Almost stuff container with scarf

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym for stuff is dropped

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
a vat is a large container for liquids

explanation.surface: Something stuffed nearly full inside a container along with a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts CRAM to CRA; 'with' just joins it to VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a wide neckband worn like a short scarf tucked into a shirt collar.

clue.text: No-go signal led off in grip of Conservatives

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it

parts.note: the right is the conservative wing of politics

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stop signal was set off while Tories held power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led off' reads like being escorted away, but 'off' is the anagram signal, and 'in grip of' is the container signal. The political right is the conservative side.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic light orders vehicles to stop, so it is a signal saying do not go.

clue.text: Compete eagerly in Riviera

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Contestants battle keenly on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters inside 'Riviera'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to strive hard against rivals, so it means to compete eagerly.

clue.text: When speaking, becomes more tense with giants

indicators.note: when speaking signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something that tightens becomes tauter or more tense

explanation.surface: Someone grows more nervous when talking with very big people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When speaking' means TIGHTENS, said aloud, gives the answer; 'with' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, and the word now means giants generally.

clue.text: Use a chair — it's broken

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning not to sit on a broken chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ITS (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Using a chair in its normal way means resting on it, so the phrase is a way of saying be seated.

clue.text: Most dependable plan stateside

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange, so the letters of the next word are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An American scheme judged to be the most reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' signals arranging the letters of STATESIDE afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very steady can be relied on, so the superlative of steady means most dependable.

clue.text: Romantic departure made from one temple

indicators.note: made from means built out of these materials, so the letters of the words after are reworked

explanation.surface: Lovers run off from a temple to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' rearranges ONE plus TEMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping means running away secretly to marry, so it is a departure made for love.

clue.text: Cards' winning serves

definitions.meaning: playing cards of the highest rank, each marked with a single pip
in tennis, services the receiver cannot touch, winning the point outright

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the top-ranking playing cards and unreturnable tennis services, a double definition.

clue.text: Kingdom has a party? Then put short skirt on

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a mini is a very short skirt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone throwing a party in their realm decides to wear a miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'Then put' only join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominion is a territory under a sovereign's rule, a synonym for a kingdom or realm.

clue.text: Publican has part of castle in more central surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means placed around, so the second word wraps the first

parts.note: inner means nearer the centre
the keep is the main fortified tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A pub landlord has a bit of a castle as a more central part of his premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' is the container signal; 'has' only links. A publican is a British pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs an inn or pub, which is what a publican does.

clue.text: Get realm entangled in wire

indicators.note: entangled means twisted up, so the letters of the two words before are mixed

explanation.surface: A kingdom gets caught up in a length of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' rearranges GET plus REALM; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is an old informal word for a telegram, a message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Kipling character has shaken her badly

indicators.note: badly suggests things done wrong, so the letters of the two preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A character from Kipling has rattled a woman severely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SHAKEN plus HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Shere Khan is the tiger who is Mowgli's enemy in Kipling's The Jungle Book, a character from his stories.

clue.text: Begin growing wild lilac from France

indicators.note: begin points to the start of the next word
wild means out of control, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gardener starts cultivating some wild lilac from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin' gives G from 'growing', and 'wild' rearranges LILAC into ALLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic means French, from Gaul, the ancient Roman name for the region of France.

clue.text: Take in muscles or brawn at first

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder takes in muscles or strength to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives B from 'brawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or assimilate, so it means to take in.

clue.text: Read news out having given reply

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads the news aloud after giving a response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges READ plus NEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given a reply to a question is to have responded to it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Place thyme, perhaps, in another basket

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: An instruction to put some thyme into a second basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters running across 'another basket'; 'perhaps' marks thyme as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a culinary herb, so it is an example of the category, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Finally examine gene code of woman

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: DNA is the molecule carrying the genetic code

explanation.surface: A last check of a woman's genetic code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives E from 'examine'; 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Fifty-one scolded harshly, but given freedom

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
to berate is to scold someone harshly

explanation.surface: Fifty-one people were told off severely yet still set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To be liberated is to be set free from confinement, a synonym for being granted liberty.

clue.text: Insect said to exist

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A creature that is said to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' means BE, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is a flying insect that makes honey, so it is an example of an insect.

clue.text: In favour of support for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all of it, so the last letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: a prop is a support

explanation.surface: Someone mostly backing a supportive position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims PROP to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pro something means being for it, the Latin preposition meaning in favour of.

clue.text: The best, yes, is rich and smooth

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop
Y is a common abbreviation for yes, as in Y/N

explanation.surface: A connoisseur agrees the finest product is luxurious and silky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with the texture of dairy cream is luscious and velvety, so it is rich and smooth.

clue.text: Unknown barge travelling to capital city

parts.note: in algebra, x, y and z stand for unknown quantities, so Z can mean unknown

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mysterious barge on its way to a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' is the anagram signal; 'to' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, so it is one example of a national capital city.
